headline: THIS IS HOW A
FENCE *GOES IN*
beats.vo: This is how a fence goes in. It starts with the *posts*.
Before any post hole, request a free *B.C. One Call* locate, at least three business days ahead.

headline: ABOUT *1/3* IN
THE GROUND
beats.vo: *Rule of thumb*: about a *third* of the post goes in the ground. For a six foot fence, *two to three feet*.

headline: GRAVEL UNDER.
*CROWN* THE TOP.
beats.vo: *Gravel* underneath lets water drain, and the concrete gets *crowned* so rain runs off.

headline: POSTS EVERY
*6-8 FT*
beats.vo: And posts usually go every *six to eight feet*.

post.caption: How a fence should be installed in Metro Vancouver, starting with the posts: request a free BC 1 Call locate before you dig, set about a third of the post in the ground (2-3 ft for a 6 ft fence), put gravel underneath, crown the concrete so rain runs off, and space posts 6-8 ft apart. Rules of thumb; every site is different.
post.alt: A framed cedar fence panel between two capped posts, an animated diagram of a wood fence post footing with gravel and crowned concrete, and a finished cedar fence along a street.
